chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out on the Day of Sacrifice to the rear of the city upon a camel that was bare-backed (without a saddle). So he passed by the women, stopped by them, and then said: 'O group of women! Give charity and obey your husbands, for most of you will be in the Fire.'

When they heard that, they wept. Then a woman from among them stood up to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! In the Fire along with the disbelievers? By Allah, we are not disbelievers, so we should become from the inhabitants of the Fire.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'You are disbelievers by virtue of the rights of your husbands.'

key_terms.كَافِرَاتٌ بِحَقِّ أَزْوَاجِكُنَّ: Disbelievers by virtue of the rights of your husbands
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean when he tells women they are 'disbelievers' in relation to their husbands?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the theological weight of marital obedience by linking women's spiritual fate to their conduct toward husbands, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding 'nushuz' (disobedience). The Prophet’s clarification that 'kufr' here denotes 'kufr al-a'mal' (disbelief of action) rather than 'kufr al-i'tiqad' (disbelief of creed) prevents misunderstanding of their eternal status, while the setting on Eid al-Adhar underscores the communal obligation of charity alongside domestic duties.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Ghalib, from Jabir Al Ju’fy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> went out on the day of the sacrifice (10<sup>th</sup> Zilhajj), to the back of Al-Medina upon a bare camel. So he<sup>saww</sup> passed by the women, and he<sup>saww</sup> paused above them, then said: ‘O group of women! You should give charity, and obey your husbands, for most of you would be in the Fire’.

So when they heard that, they wept. Then a woman from them stood up to him<sup>saww</sup> and said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! In the Fire along with the disbelievers? By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, we are not with disbelievers, so we should come to be from the inhabitants of the Fire’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said to her: ‘They are the ones who denied the rights of their husbands’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ghalib from Jabir al-Juhfiy who has said the following:

“Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once on the tenth of the month of Dhul al-Hajj the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, moved out of the city of al-Madinah toward the backside of it on a camel without a saddle and passed by women, stopped higher than them and said, ‘O community of women, you must give charity and obey your husbands; the majority of you will be in the fire.’

When they heard it they wept and one woman from them stood up and asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, will we be in the fire with the unbelievers? By Allah, we are not unbelievers to be punished and to become of the people of the fire.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘This will happen if you deny the rights of your husbands.’”
